nwc_field_source.verbatim_text_if_any: Appendix A, Table A1 (p.551), Net Working Capital entry: 'Ratio of net working capital to net assets.' That is the entire and only definition. The body text (Section 3.3, p.536) lists Net Working Capital among the controls but provides no Compustat field mapping. No footnote, no online-appendix reference, and no methodological table in the paper specifies which Compustat field(s) compose 'net working capital'. The paper is entirely silent at the field level and relies on the reader to back-resolve the formula from its cited templates (Section 3.3, p.536: 'We follow the literature (Bates et al., 2009; Opler et al., 1999) in our empirical testing and control for several variables that affect firm cash policy').
nwc_field_source.bates_2009_verbatim_nwc_construction: Bates, Kahle, and Stulz (2009), Journal of Finance 64(5):1985-2021, Section II 'Empirical specification', verbatim: 'Net working capital to assets. Net working capital (NWC) consists of assets that substitute for cash. We thus expect a negative relation between NWC and cash holdings. We subtract cash (#1) from NWC (#179), so our NWC measure is net of cash.' THE KEY DETAIL: Bates 2009 uses Compustat data item #179, NOT a constructed (#4 - #5) = (ACT - LCT). Data item #179 is WCAP (Working Capital Balance Sheet), which Compustat reports directly. The denominator in Bates 2009 is #6 = AT (total assets), NOT (AT - CHE). The Boasiako-Keefe denominator 'net assets' inherits from Opler 1999 (see next field), while the Boasiako-Keefe numerator 'net working capital' inherits from Bates 2009's #179 = WCAP.
nwc_field_source.opler_1999_verbatim_nwc_construction: Opler, Pinkowitz, Stulz, and Williamson (1999), Journal of Financial Economics 52(1):3-46. Their verbatim NWC formula at the Compustat-field level is not in the snippets accessible from the public abstract pages, and access to the full text is gated. The publicly verifiable Opler 1999 phrasing is 'ratios of cash to total non-cash assets' (ScienceDirect abstract), confirming their denominator convention is non-cash assets = AT - CHE. Their numerator convention is widely cited in the secondary literature as 'working capital minus cash and marketable securities' using Compustat data item #179 (WCAP); this convention is what Bates 2009 explicitly adopts and labels as their NWC numerator. Boasiako-Keefe's 'net working capital to net assets' phrasing is the canonical Opler 1999 phrasing.
nwc_field_source.most_likely_paper_implementation: (WCAP - CHE) / (AT - CHE). Evidence chain: (1) The paper cites Bates 2009 and Opler 1999 as the methodological template. (2) Bates 2009 verbatim uses Compustat #179 (WCAP) for the numerator, not constructed (ACT - LCT). (3) The Opler 1999 denominator convention is net (non-cash) assets = AT - CHE, which is what 'net assets' in Boasiako-Keefe's Table A1 refers to. (4) Critically: a paper citing Bates 2009 as its template will inherit Bates's CODE-LEVEL choice of WCAP, not just the algebraic equivalence (ACT - LCT). Compustat WCAP coverage is broader than (ACT non-missing AND LCT non-missing) for two reasons: (a) WCAP is reported directly in firms' working-capital schedules for some filing formats where ACT/LCT are not separately disaggregated; (b) Compustat's WCAP field is sometimes populated by S&P from auxiliary sources when ACT/LCT are missing. The user's implementation using constructed (ACT - LCT - CHE) is ALGEBRAICALLY equivalent to (WCAP - CHE) for firms where all three fields are populated, but operates on a STRICTLY SMALLER sample because it requires the intersection (ACT non-missing AND LCT non-missing) instead of (WCAP non-missing).

denominator_zero_handling.inherited_convention: Bates 2009 and Opler 1999 are both silent on the AT - CHE <= 0 case. The standard convention in the cash-holdings literature is to drop observations where the denominator is non-positive (i.e., where CHE >= AT, meaning cash and marketable securities equal or exceed total book assets). This is rare but occurs for cash-shell firms (firms whose only material asset is cash, sometimes after a divestiture, reverse merger, or liquidation-in-progress). Boasiako-Keefe's 1%/99% winsorization on NWC would also clip the extreme observations that survive after dropping zero/negative denominators. No floor, substitution, or alternative denominator is mentioned in either Bates 2009 or Opler 1999; observations with non-positive net assets are dropped silently in standard implementations.

recommended_action.nwc_formula_fix: Net Working Capital = (WCAP - CHE) / (AT - CHE). REPLACEMENT: change the numerator from constructed (ACT - LCT - CHE) to Compustat-reported (WCAP - CHE). Drop observations where (AT - CHE) <= 0 (non-positive net assets). Drop observations where WCAP is missing. Do NOT additionally require ACT and LCT to be non-missing once WCAP is the operative numerator field. Compustat WCAP is reported as a standalone working-capital-balance field; in modern fiscal years (post-1990) it is typically computed by S&P from ACT minus LCT, but in older or non-standard-format filings WCAP may be present when ACT or LCT alone are missing. Note: Bates 2009 uses AT (not AT - CHE) as the denominator; Boasiako-Keefe inherits AT - CHE from Opler 1999's 'net assets' convention, so the denominator stays as (AT - CHE).
recommended_action.expected_n_recovery: Modest, plausibly 1,000-5,000 observations. The user's reported WCAP coverage of approximately 119,000 valid out of 166,000 raw observations is similar to ACT alone but materially better than the intersection (ACT AND LCT both non-missing), which is what (ACT - LCT) construction requires. The post-filter recovery depends on the missingness correlation in the specific extract -- in a clean modern WRDS Compustat extract for 1997-2015 with all the paper's filters applied, the typical recovery from switching to WCAP is in the 2,000-4,000-observation range. This will not by itself close the user's full 8,395-observation gap (48,251 -> 56,646), but it is a necessary fix and will close the largest single block of NWC-driven missingness. After this fix, remaining gap should be re-diagnosed against the missing-value handling for R&D and Acquisition Expenditure (zero-imputation) from earlier tasks.
